title: The affected selection as the task gate
desiredOutcome: A task's gate is the affected selection, after a re-measurement shows 0 misses over at least 20 commits; whole-tree scanners run once per phase and on push; CI stays inside its wall-time bound

findings.issue: contradicts task clause: "`time python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py` must finish in under 240 s wall on the owner's machine, twice, at least 20 minutes apart, on a quiet machine" (and the title, 'The sweep finishes under four minutes'). The diff does not meet it: the executor's own runs are 378.4 s and 492.3 s wall on a loaded machine (load 10-49), 519.5 s before, and its estimate for a quiet machine is 280-300 s. The task's own fallback clause ('If 240 s is still out of reach, say what the remaining critical path is ... and do not close the task as met') applies, and the executor does follow it: it does not claim the target and names the critical path (production git calls, measured as 10104 child processes in ar-block; other suites). So the report is honest, but the task as titled is NOT met and must not be closed as met.
findings.resolution: fixed in P143.7-z9j (d1a877b79e51): Close this task as partial (the in-process conversion and the split of ar-block), not as meeting 240 s. File a follow-up task that (a) memoises or batches the production git calls the profile named (_config.checkout_top / rev-parse per call, integrate-task refresh_records, drive-phase carry_git/tree_undescribed, _worktrees.admin_dir, _locks.lock_dir) and/or cuts the next-heaviest suites (test_audit_task, test_commit_task_work, test_stamp_verification, test__deps, test_close_phase), and (b) owns the two timed quiet-machine runs 20 minutes apart, since none of the five timed runs here was quiet.

findings.issue: The new runner is shared by almost every case in the suite, yet the five-row probe mutates the verbs and the sitecustomize fallback, never the runner itself. Nothing shown goes red if _restore_environ stops removing a verb's added variables (the lock token it hands children), if cwd or sys.argv are not restored, or if _exit_status maps a non-int exit code to 0. Process-global state leaking from one verb into the next is the one defect class in-process execution adds, and tests.add is none. Related fidelity gap: in-process the lock holder pid recorded by _locks._holder_pid is the live test process (and _locks.py:577 treats pid == getpid() as ours), so a case that depends on a lock left by a verb that died being read as holder-gone cannot be shown through an in-process verb. No row shows such a case still spawns a process.
findings.resolution: Add a small case in the suite (and a probe row each) that runs a stub script through _run_in_process which sets an environment variable, changes cwd, calls sys.exit('x') and sys.exit(3), and assert the environment, cwd, argv and exit codes after; and add a probe row that makes the runner leak the environment. For the pid point, either grep the converted cases for ones that rely on a verb's own pid being dead and route them through _needs_process, or state in the runner comment that holder-liveness is not exercised in-process.

findings.issue: The task said to re-record the figures the executor measured. The 120 block figures were not recorded by --record-costs; they were derived by scaling the darwin block seconds of one loaded run (run2, load 10-24) by 4913.6/2080.0, the old windows-latest suite figure over the darwin seconds of the baseline run (load 20-26). The three new blocks (ar5/ar9/ar18) and the suite figure 2665.5 therefore rest on two runs taken under different machine loads. These figures set per-block hang-detector timeouts and shard balance in CI, so an under-estimate on windows shows up as a spurious timeout and an over-estimate only as a slack deadline. It is disclosed in the platform note, and swd7 and bk5/tt5 are green.

findings.issue: The new test-support widening ignores a declared entry that is the unscoped sweep. select() returns `widen` for any changed file under a test directory that no arm picked, whatever the task's gate holds, so affected_steps never reaches left_to_run and instead adds every phase-gate entry the task did not declare as `affected/phase-gate:` steps. With a gate of [selftests] (or [selftests, lint]) in the dogfood plan, a change to tests/_harness.py now pulls validate, plugin-validate, gate, report, shots, interactive and vitest into the task run, browser gates included. But the reason for this widening is that every suite may depend on the support file, and `selftests` (python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py, the spelling with {paths} removed) already runs every suite. This works against the description's 'counts as already wide for the Python arm' and the phase outcome that whole-tree scanners run once per phase. It costs time but is not a correctness gap: the widened run is a superset.
findings.resolution: Treat the test-support widen as satisfied when a declared entry is the derived spelling with `{paths}` removed. That is the same word comparison left_to_run makes. Either have select() report support as its own reason (e.g. `widenSuites`) that affected_steps checks against the declared entries before adding the phase gate, or make the check in affected_steps. Add a case: gate [selftests] with only tests/_harness.py changed adds no phase-gate step and says which key covers it. Keep the case where a narrow path-scoped gate with the same change still widens.

findings.issue: Suppose the combined `--show-toplevel` + fields question is refused and a repository stands above. git_place then asks a second time for the fields alone, whatever the refusal was, including a TimeoutExpired or a failure to start git. That doubles the worst-case wait. A hook path that asks a field list without --show-toplevel (`_shares_repository` and `path_tree` ask `--git-common-dir` alone) can now spend 5 s + 5 s, which equals the 10 s timeout hooks.json gives every hook. A killed guard lets the call through. In _worktrees the wait goes from 60 s to 120 s.
findings.resolution: Retry the fields-alone question only when the first refusal is git's bare/no-work-tree refusal: the reason line names a work tree, or a separate rev-parse --is-bare-repository says so. Do not retry on a timeout or an exception. Or hand the second ask whatever is left of the first one's timeout. Add a case with a stub `_ask_rev_parse` that times out and assert that it was called once.

findings.issue: The two witnesses check different things. A kept refusal is dropped when a bare-repository shape (HEAD + objects + refs) appears on the way up. A kept answer only checks for `.git` entries between the directory and its top (_inside_known_tree) and the identity of top/.git. So a kept answer survives two kinds of change. (a) A bare repository initialised in a directory between the asked directory and its top: git would then refuse or answer the bare repo, but the memo still hands back the old top. (b) A config-only change under an unchanged `.git` directory, such as `core.worktree` or `core.bare` set after the answer was kept. A directory's inode does not move when .git/config is edited. Both are rare, and a hook is one process per call. The drive process is long-lived, though, and the block comment says the witness covers 'a repository initialised between the directory and the top it had' without that limit.
findings.resolution: Have the answer witness walk with the same predicate as _no_repository_above, so the bare shape counts too. When top/.git is a directory, add .git/config's (st_ino, st_size, st_mtime_ns) to its identity. Otherwise state both limits in the block comment above _STANDING_FIELDS. Do not add GIT_CONFIG_COUNT to _DISCOVERY_ENV: the sweep runner sets it for every child, which would turn the memo off under test.

findings.issue: The re-recorded table changes how a dependant behaves, not just how much time it holds back. stamp-verification.py's `red` reads the same table to size a sweep-shaped red-first command, and fit_problem() refuses to start any run when 3 x the schedule wall exceeds the deadline (capped at MAX_TIMEOUT 565). I computed it with the module's own sized_deadline/fit_problem, on this 10-core host (8 workers), for `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_drive_phase.py`. With the darwin table at HEAD, need is 324 s and the command fits. With the new Windows table, need is 1011 s against a 565 s deadline, so it REFUSES ('no run was started'). Other suites also grew several-fold: test__worktrees need 123 -> 492, test__manifest_io 15 -> 399. They still fit, but close to the cap. So on the developer's machine, a red-first proof naming the drive's suite now ends in could-not-prove, because Windows figures are being read as darwin wall time. The executor's dependant answer ('holds back more time') understates this.
findings.resolution: fixed in P143.9-z9j (9aeecd5a2c27): This table is right for CI, which binds on Windows, so keep it. Fix the reader in a follow-up task on stamp-verification.py: have sweep_wall compare the table's `platform` with the host and not treat another platform's figures as this host's wall time. Either scale them, or count the need as unmeasured, with the basis naming the platform mismatch, so fit_problem does not refuse on borrowed figures. Add a case that goes red when a windows-recorded table refuses a darwin proof. Until then, correct the dependant answer in the return to say that the drive suite's sweep-shaped red-first proof now refuses on this host.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'Split the serial manifest-validation job ... into verify.sh slices that run as parallel jobs' and acceptance (1) 'the median wall of at least five per-run CI runs is at most 8 minutes and their median runner-minutes at most 55'. The split was not made: verify.sh is untouched. Acceptance (1) is not met. One run exists at d1a877b7 (41070108164, release-tier workflow_dispatch, success). I measured its per-run jobs, resample excluded, with `gh run view --json jobs`: wall 9.9 min (14:14:32 -> 14:24:27) and 106.3 runner-minutes (117 if billed per started minute). The 8 Windows selftests cells alone sum to 66.6 min (cp1252 leg 34.8), the linux cells to 23.0, and linux stress to 11.6. The critical path is selftests (windows, cp1252 4) at 581 s. Two Windows plain cells started late (14:15:23 and 14:16:07), which looks like a concurrent-job cap. One run is also not the five-run median the clause asks for. For comparison, the previous dispatch at c185b4cb (40946289828) was 14.1 min and 146.7 runner-minutes, so this is an improvement but not the target.
findings.resolution: Do not close the task as meeting its acceptance. The executor's case against the split holds: the manifests+js+plugin job ran 49 s, off a 581 s critical path, and each extra job adds about 12 s of setup plus a queue slot. The owner should amend the clause rather than force the split. Neither target can be met by job shape. Rebalanced on the new table, a Windows cell is about 498 s of sweep plus about 60 s of setup, which is still over 8 min. 55 runner-minutes is below the 66.6 the Windows cells take alone. Meeting them needs a follow-up that cuts the Windows sweep's CPU (test_drive_phase 2688, test_commit_task_work 665, test_audit_task 629, test_close_phase 470 and test_stamp_verification 462 slot-seconds), or an owner decision to drop legs (the Windows cp1252 leg is 34.8 runner-minutes). After that, take at least five per-run runs at the rebalanced table to measure the median.

findings.issue: fx2 and fx3 check that a copy is correct. Nothing checks that the copy (the task's only cut) actually happens. If _repo built every fixture fresh, or if _REPO_TEMPLATES never returned a hit (a mutation that drops the cache), fx2 and fx3 would both stay green. That makes the saving silently revertible. The executor's probe rows M1-M5 all mutate correctness, never whether the template is reused.
findings.resolution: Add a case that calls _repo twice with the same arguments and asserts that the second call did not grow _REPO_TEMPLATES (or did not run `git init`, e.g. through the suite's existing counting shim). Prove it red by mutating `_REPO_TEMPLATES[files] = template` away.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "keep behaviour identical": _phase_entry used `rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` and now uses head_sha, whose _ask_head runs plain `git rev-parse HEAD`. On an unborn branch with a root entry named HEAD, git exits 0 and prints the literal string "HEAD". On macOS's case-insensitive filesystem a `head` or `Head` file or directory has the same effect. `--verify -q` exits 1 in that case. head_sha returns "HEAD" even though its docstring says it returns 'the commit HEAD names, or None'. `start` then skips the 'has no commit yet ... commit first' refusal and returns state cut with baseRef "HEAD". The memo cannot catch this: _files_head returns None for an unborn branch, so the answer comes straight from git. Reproduced in scratchpad/p14310/rev/headfile2.sh (unborn plus `head` file: plain exit 0 'HEAD'; plus `Head` directory: exit 0 'HEAD'; with nothing there: exit 128) and in rev/probe_head.py case 11 (head_sha='HEAD', --verify=None). The existing case pe6 (tests/test_audit_task.py:9682) builds an unborn repo with no such entry, so it stays green.
findings.resolution: Have _ask_head ask `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`, and have head_sha return None unless the answer matches _OBJECT_NAME. That also makes drive-phase.git_head stricter in the same edge, where it is already pre-existing. Add an sc-hd case with an unborn repo holding a `head` directory, asserting None, and confirm it is red against the plain spelling.

findings.issue: _ref_file returns b"" both for a missing file and for an existing zero-length file, so a zero-length loose ref counts as 'no loose file' and packed-refs answers. Git refuses that ref as broken; this is the empty-ref-after-power-loss state. Once a process has memoised the packed answer, head_sha keeps returning that commit while git returns nothing. Probe case 3 in rev/probe_head.py: head_sha='4e7928d2...', git=None. Git never writes this state itself (it uses lock-and-rename), so it needs a corrupt repository.
findings.resolution: Tell missing apart from empty. Have _ref_file return b"" only on FileNotFoundError/NotADirectoryError and None for an existing empty file, so _files_head returns None and git is asked.

findings.issue: The _tracking docstring claims 'the same answer one listing each would give', and two shapes break it. (a) A trailing-slash spec naming a gitlink: `sm/` against a submodule `sm` is tracked when asked alone and untracked when batched, because _spec_holds requires `path.startswith('sm/')` and git lists `sm`. (b) GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS=1 in the environment: `Docs`, `DOCS/x.txt` and `.Claude/a.json` are tracked when asked alone and untracked when batched. Both come from rev/probe_head.py section 13. The one caller, plugin_owned_rels, asks only CONFIG_NAME and GITIGNORE_NAME as fixed lower-case file paths, so neither shape is reachable today. The claim is still wider than the code.
findings.resolution: Have _plain_pathspec refuse a spec ending in '/' and refuse batching whenever GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS is set, so those are asked alone. Alternatively, narrow the docstring to the shapes the matcher reproduces.

tasks.title: A task's gate is the affected selection, and no derived step re-runs what a declared key already runs in full
tasks.description: run-test-gate.py measures a task's declared non-suite entries plus the suites the selection names for its changed paths; an unrecognised path class widens to the phase gate and says so. A declared key whose command is the unscoped sweep (the dogfood plan's selftests) counts as already wide for the Python arm, so no affected/python or affected/related step is added beside it: today such steps re-run suites the key already ran. The recorded row commits with no override. Acceptance: (1) a task gate holding the full-sweep key adds no affected/python or affected/related step; (2) a narrow declared gate gets the affected suites for its changed paths and none for an unchanged tree; (3) an unrecognised path widens to the phase gate, saying so; (4) the green row commits without override; (5) the selection is used only after the miss-rate task's result is recorded with zero misses, or with each miss's path class widened to the full set.

tasks.description:
The previous task moved the drive suite's verbs in-process (child CPU of a full sweep down about 22-24 percent, longest job from about 304 s to about 94 s), but a full `time python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py` still took 378-502 s on a loaded machine, against the target of under 240 s. Do:
1. Measure first (choosing-what-to-optimize): rank the callers by the git time they cause across a whole sweep, not one block, and say which ones pay.
2. Cut the calls that pay: one shared, explicitly invalidated memo for answers that cannot change within one process (a checkout's top level, its git dir, a worktree's admin dir), or a batched call where one git invocation can answer several questions. One mechanism shared by every caller, not a per-caller cache; a cached answer must never outlive a change that can alter it (a worktree added or removed, a checkout moved), and the case for that is red-first.
3. If the target still needs it, cut the next-heaviest suites' wall (test_audit_task, test_commit_task_work, test_stamp_verification, test__deps, test_close_phase) by the same rule, measured.

The drive-phase carry path (carry_git: ls-files/diff/status/update-index on a scratch index) asks things that change between calls, so it is not memoisable.

(1) hooks/_config.py: one shared place memo behind the one door git_place(cwd, fields, timeout) -> (answers, why), with _git_rev_parse as its answers-only wrapper and _ask_rev_parse as the raw process. Only place fields are kept, keyed by (cwd, realpath, fields). Each answer is stored beside a witness that is re-read from disk before every reuse: the identity of the top's .git entry (a dir by dev/ino; a gitfile by dev/ino/size/mtime_ns) plus no .git between the directory and its top (_inside_known_tree). A refusal is kept only while no repository (a .git entry or a bare HEAD/objects/refs dir) stands anywhere above. An environment steering discovery (GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES, GIT_DISCOVERY_ACROSS_FILESYSTEM) bypasses the memo. A bare repository falls back to asking for the fields alone. forget_git_standing() clears the memo. tasks.title: fix P143-R13: contradicts task clause "keep behaviour identical": _phase_entr...
tasks.description:
contradicts task clause "keep behaviour identical": _phase_entry used `rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` and now uses head_sha, whose _ask_head runs plain `git rev-parse HEAD`. On an unborn branch with a root entry named HEAD, git exits 0 and prints the literal string "HEAD". On macOS's case-insensitive filesystem a `head` or `Head` file or directory has the same effect. `--verify -q` exits 1 in that case. head_sha returns "HEAD" even though its docstring says it returns 'the commit HEAD names, or None'. `start` then skips the 'has no commit yet ... commit first' refusal and returns state cut with baseRef "HEAD". The memo cannot catch this: _files_head returns None for an unborn branch, so the answer comes straight from git. Reproduced in scratchpad/p14310/rev/headfile2.sh (unborn plus `head` file: plain exit 0 'HEAD'; plus `Head` directory: exit 0 'HEAD'; with nothing there: exit 128) and in rev/probe_head.py case 11 (head_sha='HEAD', --verify=None). The existing case pe6 (tests/test_audit_task.py:9682) builds an unborn repo with no such entry, so it stays green.

Resolution asked: Have _ask_head ask `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`, and have head_sha return None unless the answer matches _OBJECT_NAME. That also makes drive-phase.git_head stricter in the same edge, where it is already pre-existing. Add an sc-hd case with an unborn repo holding a `head` directory, asserting None, and confirm it is red against the plain spelling.
